title: Cyrus and the Safehouse
premise: Cyrus Winterbourne, a deniable hostage negotiator haunted by the one exchange that ended in blood, is summoned when Flight 447 to Frankfurt vanishes from every radar, manifest, and database while still airborne. Aboard are a whistleblower carrying proof of a trilateral money-laundering scheme, and an assassin whose employer wants both the man and the plane erased. As Cyrus negotiates with hijackers, spooks, and her own agency's handlers, she discovers the 'failure' on her record was engineered by the same network, and that the assassin is someone she once loved and lost. She trades her career, her cover identity, and nearly her life to land the truth in Frankfurt before markets open, ending with the whistleblower testifying, the network exposed but its principals scattered, and Cyrus walking away from the service that made her — finally owning her real name.
about_author: Juniper Coldharbour spent a decade writing risk assessments for insurance syndicates before turning to fiction, a career she describes as 'negotiation with worse dialogue.' She lives off-grid on the Baltic coast, where she claims the fog improves her plotting.

chapters.title: The Board
chapters.summary: Cyrus Winterbourne's POV. In a windowless Vienna annex, Cyrus closes a hostage case no one will credit her for, while her handler dangles the one file she's never been allowed to read: her own failure in Marseilles. Emotional beat: professional control masking old grief.

chapters.title: Ghost Altitude
chapters.summary: Air traffic controller Marek Dvořák's POV. Flight 447 blinks off every screen over the Alps mid-flight; his queries are stonewalled within minutes. He keeps a screenshot he shouldn't have. Emotional beat: creeping dread as institutional silence replaces answers.

chapters.title: Attribution Denied
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She's activated under a deniable mandate: find the plane, find the whistleblower aboard, tell no one. She recognizes the operation's shape — it mirrors Marseilles. Emotional beat: unease hardening into suspicion of her own employers.

chapters.title: The Passenger Manifest That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with intercut whistleblower Elias Brandt's smuggled audio diary. She reconstructs the passenger list from boarding-gate footage and finds a name redacted at source: hers, from six years ago. Emotional beat: vertigo — the past has been riding along all along.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Cyrus negotiates a joint-access meeting between German, Austrian, and French liaisons who each deny ownership of the crisis while blocking her exits. Emotional beat: chess-like tension; she realizes all three governments already know something.

chapters.title: What Elias Carried
chapters.summary: Elias Brandt's POV, flashback-structured. The encrypted ledger he swallowed into a data chip: shell companies routing arms money through Frankfurt clearing houses, signed off by officials in all three capitals. Emotional beat: terrified resolve of a man who chose truth over safety.

chapters.title: The Man Who Answers to Vesper
chapters.summary: Assassin Vesper's POV. Introduced mid-execution of a bank auditor in Zurich; elegant, methodical, and carrying a photograph of Cyrus he shouldn't have. Emotional beat: cold professionalism cracked by one unprofessional keepsake.

chapters.title: Landing Rights
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The plane lands at a closed military strip; passengers are held as 'material witnesses.' Cyrus talks her way inside using a dead man's credentials. Emotional beat: audacity laced with fear of being disappeared herself.

chapters.title: Six Years Ago
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Cyrus and Vesper. Interleaved memories of Sarajevo, where they were lovers and colleagues before the mission that broke them — the mission now filed as her failure. Emotional beat: love remembered as both wound and evidence.

chapters.title: The Negotiation Room
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Face to face with the detained whistleblower, she must decide whether to protect him or use him. Her handler orders option two. Emotional beat: duty and conscience pulling in opposite directions for the first time on the record.

chapters.title: Vesper Makes Contact
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A note in her hotel room, in handwriting only one person alive knows: 'You were right about Marseilles.' Emotional beat: shock curdling into fury — the assassin is Daniel, presumed dead.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Opens at Nine
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation (Marek, a Bundesbank analyst, a journalist). The financial world senses blood in the water; short positions stack against the exposed banks. Clock starts ticking in earnest. Emotional beat: mounting systemic dread.

chapters.title: The Handler's Ledger
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She breaks into her own agency's archive and reads the true Marseilles file: her failure was manufactured to burn an asset who knew too much — Daniel. Emotional beat: betrayal as revelation; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Daniel/Vesper's POV. He explains why he faked his death and took the contract: the only way to get close enough to kill the network's architect. He offers Cyrus the shot instead. Emotional beat: love against duty, stated plainly at last.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Committee
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Hauled before the three governments' liaison panel, she plays their denials back at them with Elias's ledger as leverage, buying twelve hours and Elias's transfer. Emotional beat: the negotiator negotiating for her own soul.

chapters.title: Extraction Interrupted
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The transfer convoy is ambushed by the network's contractors; Marek's screenshot becomes the breadcrumb that lets Cyrus intercept. Emotional beat: desperate momentum, allies assembled from strangers.

chapters.title: The Architect
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Confrontation with Deputy Director Halvorsen — her mentor, the network's banker of secrets, who offers her Daniel's head in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: the seductive logic of complicity, refused.

chapters.title: Night Over the Main
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating Cyrus/Daniel POV. On a Frankfurt rooftop above the pre-market exchanges, Halvorsen's cleaners close in; Daniel takes a bullet meant for Cyrus, and she chooses truth over the exit offered, broadcasting the ledger live. Emotional beat: sacrifice and irrevocable choice.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: Journalist Anke Roth's POV. The ledger hits every terminal at 9:00 a.m.; three currencies wobble, two ministers resign, and the story outruns every attempt to bury it. Emotional beat: chaotic, exhilarating vindication.

chapters.title: What the Record Shows
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Testimony rooms, leaked transcripts, and the slow machinery of accountability; Daniel survives, barely, under new custody. Her Marseilles file is corrected — quietly, without apology. Emotional beat: justice as process, not fireworks.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She walks out of the annex, declining reassignment, leaving her cover names behind like coats. A final scene with Daniel across a table, no handlers present. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace.

chapters.title: Cyrus Winterbourne
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Cyrus's POV. On the Baltic coast, under a name that is simply hers, she receives one last redacted file — and burns it unread. Emotional beat: identity reclaimed; loyalty finally aligned with truth.
